question:
Identify the following reactions as precipitation, neutralisation, redox, addition, or decomposition:
(a) $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4(aq) + \text{CuO}(s) \longrightarrow \text{CuSO}_4(aq) + \text{H}_2\text{O}(l)$
(b) $\text{Mg}(s) + \text{I}_2(g) \longrightarrow \text{MgI}_2(s)$
(c) $\text{BaCl}_2(aq) + \text{K}_2\text{SO}_4(aq) \longrightarrow \text{BaSO}_4(s) + 2\text{KCl}(aq)$
(d) $\text{PbO}_2(aq) + \text{SO}_2(g) \longrightarrow \text{PbSO}_4(s)$
(e) $\text{Pb(NO}_3)_2(aq) + 2\text{KI}(aq) \longrightarrow 2\text{KNO}_3(aq) + \text{PbI}_2(s)$
List five uses of compounds of group 2 elements of the periodic table.
Using an appropriate equation(s), explain why an aqueous solution of $\text{AlCl}_3$ is acidic to litmus paper.
A $1.00\text{ dm}^3$ vessel contains oxygen gas at $25^\circ\text{C}$ and a pressure of $4.05 \times 10^5\text{ Pascals}$. Calculate the number of molecules of oxygen present in the vessel.

Give the shapes of the following species:
(a) $\text{NH}_3$
(b) $\text{NH}_4^+$
(c) $\text{BCl}_3$
(d) $\text{CO}_2$
(e) $\text{H}_2\text{O}$
State Le-Chatelier's principle.

Lime is prepared by the decomposition of calcium trioxocarbonate(IV) at $298\text{K}$ in accordance to the equation: $\text{CaCO}_3(s) \longrightarrow \text{CaO}(s) + \text{CO}_2(g) \quad \Delta G = +31\text{kcal mol}^{-1}$
(i) Is the reaction spontaneous at $500\text{K}$?
(ii) What is the change in entropy of the reaction?
(iii) Does the reaction occur spontaneously at $298\text{K}$?

In a Victor Meyer experiment, $0.52\text{g}$ of an organic liquid of a molar mass $120\text{g mol}^{-1}$ was vapourised at a temperature of $298\text{K}$ and pressure of $1.013 \times 10^5\text{ Nm}^{-2}$. What is the volume $(\text{cm}^3)$ of the air displaced? Given that the saturated vapour pressure of water at $298\text{K}$ is $2.32 \times 10^3\text{ N m}^{-2}$.
When calcium was burnt in gas A, compound B was formed. The compound B reacted with water to form gas C which turned red litmus paper to blue. Identify A and B.
What is a battery?
Using appropriate equations, explain what happens at the electrodes of a cell in terms of redox reactions.

Explain the following terms: (15 marks)
(i) Order of reaction
(ii) Rate constant
(iii) Half life
(iv) Activation energy
(v) Activated state

In the reaction, $2\text{HI}(g) \rightleftharpoons \text{H}_2(g) + \text{I}_2(g)$
Derive an expression for the equilibrium constant in terms of the concentration of all the species in the above reaction. (3 marks)

The rate constant for the decomposition of hydrogen iodide at different temperatures are provided below:
| Rate constant, $k\text{ (dm}^3\text{ mole}^{-1}\text{ s}^{-1})$ | Temperature (K) |
| --- | --- |
| $3.75 \times 10^{-7}$ | 500 |
| $6.65 \times 10^{-6}$ | 600 |
| $1.15 \times 10^{-3}$ | 700 |
| $3.75 \times 10^{-2}$ | 800 |

Determine the value of the activation energy for the decomposition reaction from the plot of $\ln k$ against $1/T$ and obtain the value for the activation energy of the decomposition reaction. (12 marks)

State the major contribution of each of the following to the development of atomic structure: (5 marks)
(i) James Chadwick
(ii) Henri Becquerel
(iii) Michael Faraday
(iv) Robert Millikan
(v) Ernest Rutherford

In the reaction:
$$\text{MnO}_4^- + \text{Cl}^- + \text{H}^+ \longrightarrow \text{Mn}^{2+} + \text{Cl}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$
Balance the equation of the reaction. (8 marks)
What is the oxidation number of manganese in $\text{MnO}_4^-$? (1 mark)
What are the species that oxidised and reduced? (2 marks)
Use an electron configuration to illustrate how manganese is able to possess variable oxidation state in this reaction. (3 marks)
What is the role of $\text{H}^+$ in the reaction? (1 mark)

In the redox reaction:
$$\text{KClO}_3 + \text{FeSO}_4 + \text{H}^+ \longrightarrow \text{KCl} + \text{Fe}_2(\text{SO}_4)_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$
What is the number of moles of iron(III) produced, when $5.1\text{g}$ of the trioxochlorate(V) is consumed in the reaction? (5 marks)

Predict the sign of the standard entropy change in the following: (5 marks)
(i) $\text{N}_2\text{O}_{4(g)} \longrightarrow 2\text{ NO}_{2(g)} \quad \Delta H^\circ = +58.04\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$
(ii) $\text{H}_2\text{O}_{(g)} + \text{C}_{(s)} \longrightarrow \text{H}_{2(g)} + \text{CO}_{(s)} \quad \Delta H^\circ = +128.4\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$
(iii) $\text{CH}_{4(g)} + 2\text{O}_{2(g)} \longrightarrow \text{CO}_{2(g)} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}_{(g)} \quad \Delta H^\circ = -885.2\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$
(iv) $\text{C}_{(s)} + \text{O}_{2(g)} \longrightarrow \text{CO}_{2(g)} \quad \Delta H^\circ = -392.3\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$
(v) $2\text{H}_{2(g)} + \text{O}_{2(g)} \longrightarrow \text{H}_2\text{O}_{(l)} \quad \Delta H^\circ = +570.0\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$
Explain the factor that is responsible for the changes in the above a(i-v) (12 marks)

The following reaction occurs at $200^\circ\text{C}$:
$$\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH}_{(g)} \longrightarrow \text{C}_2\text{H}_{4(g)} + \text{H}_2\text{O}_{(g)} \quad \Delta H = +12\text{ kcal mol}^{-1}$$
What is the sign of $\Delta G$? (4 marks)
What is the sign of $\Delta S$? (2 marks)
What feature of the reaction can affect the sign of $\Delta S$? (2 marks)
Chloride of silicon hydrolyses readily but that of carbon does not under normal condition. (5 marks)
Although both boron and aluminium belong to the same group in the periodic table, $\text{BCl}_3$ is trigonal planar but $\text{AlCl}_3$ is tetrahedral in dimeric state. (6 marks)
The first ionisation energy of beryllium is greater than that of lithium but the second ionisation energy of lithium is higher than that of beryllium. (5 marks)
The radii, $r$ of an element, $X$ and its ions follow the order: $r_{X^+} < r_X < r_{X^-}$ (4 marks)
Nitrogen is generally unreactive at room temperature but reactive at very high temperature. (5 marks)
State four unique properties of most d-block elements. (4 marks)

Using electron configuration, explain the following:
The boiling points of potassium and chromium are $760$ and $2,665^\circ\text{C}$ respectively. (5 marks)

Using electron configuration, explain the following:
Some cobalt(II) complexes have pink colour. (5 marks)

Using electron configuration, explain the following:
$+5$ oxidation state can be obtained in vanadium. (3 marks)
Account for the magnetic property of $\text{Sc}^{3+}$, $\text{Cu}^+$, $\text{Zn}^{2+}$. (8 marks)

A is a mixture of 3 substances P, Q and R. Substance P is soluble in water and ethanol but insoluble in ether. Q is soluble in ethanol and ether but not in water. R is soluble only in ether. Explain briefly, how you will determine the percentage of P in the mixture, A. (7 marks)

The atomic numbers of 2 elements, X and Y are $37$ and $35$ respectively.
Write the electron configurations of X and Y. (4 marks)
Write the formulae of the hydrides of X and Y. (4 marks)
State and explain the type of bonding between X and Y and give the formula of the compound formed. (4 marks)

(i) will conduct electricity in the solid state?
(ii) will react violently with water?
(iii) will form an acid anhydride?
(iv) will form basic hydroxide?
(v) has catenating property?
